question: Prove that corrugation has returned between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green.
norm_question: prove that corrugation has returned between liverpool street and bethnal green

answer.text: Our audio measurements and the retrieved documents cannot show whether corrugation is present between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green because we only recorded uncalibrated sound levels, though TfL ground this section between December 2021 and May 2022.

verified_claims.text: Our audio measurements and the retrieved public documents cannot show whether rail corrugation is present between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green because we only recorded saloon audio and hold no rail roughness data for that section.

In our uncalibrated phone recordings across 11 trips, Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green averaged 0.54 dB louder than Bethnal Green to Mile End, resulting in a NO-GO verdict because the difference is below 1 dB.

TfL states that corrugation is the principal cause of noise and that rail grinding must be repeated every 6 months to a year, having ground Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street between December 2021 and May 2022.
